summary: This program sets up a signal handler to gracefully exit when interrupted, then enters an infinite loop that creates empty temporary files in an output folder every second while printing a running count. The signal handler lets you stop the program cleanly by pressing Ctrl+C instead of forcefully terminating it.

explanations.1: This function will be called whenever the program receives a SIGINT signal, which is what Ctrl+C sends to a running program.
explanations.5: This line registers our signal_handler function to be invoked whenever a SIGINT (interrupt) signal arrives, essentially saying 'when Ctrl+C is pressed, run signal_handler instead of just killing the program'.
explanations.10: mkdir creates the directory if it doesn't exist; parents=True creates any missing parent directories, and exist_ok=True means it won't error if the directory already exists.
explanations.15: This creates a unique temporary filename (using tempfile.mktemp()), extracts just the filename part (os.path.basename), and joins it to the folder path to create a full file path.
explanations.18: The 'with' statement opens the file for writing and automatically closes it when done, even if an error occurs; the 'pass' means we're not actually writing anything, just creating an empty file.
